title: Four arrangements in two days; NBC wants him slowed down
summary: Budd condenses Fred Waring scores into small-band arrangements so fast that management objects.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: So when I get home -- before this I want to tell you what my assignment was. Like he said he didn't have a budget in order to say like make me 'Sweet Georgia Brown, make

arrangement on "Indiana," make arrangement on this or that or the other. He had to go to the library and pick out things such as like what Fred Waring had done, what all of those voices and strings. And I had to condense that from all of that band back down to these pieces, trace out the melodic lines and everything and get the meat and the meaning out of the music.

So this I was doing. In other words I'm picking the score to pieces and -- well, I wanted to tell you something. At that time I was pretty fast, and I made all of these four arrangements in two days, and I took them back down to NBC and when I took them down there the man flipped. He said "wait a minute you can't do this." I said "what do you mean I can't do it?" He says, "well," he says, "where's your overtime, where's your this, where's your that? You're outwriting everybody else. We have a system here, you know."

I said, man, look, I can't be stuffed with this music for no four days, I got to get out and do about my own business, I've got to play my horn, I've got to do some other writing for other people. He said, no, we're going to have to slow you down, we're going to have to give you one or two arrangements at a time. Well, I could understand what they were talking about, but any way this made me very unhappy. So any way I'm making up my mind, I said, you
